sections.html:
Walk into 112 E. Edgewater St. in Portage, Wisconsin 53901 to reach the Columbia County Register of Deeds. Phone (608) 742-9677 or fax (608) 742-9875. The counter stays staffed from 8:00 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon, while genealogy research is held from 9:00 to 3:00.

Think of it as the county's filing cabinet for land: deeds, land contracts, mortgages, UCC filings, subdivision and condominium plats, certified survey maps, lis pendens and annexations all end up here, along with birth, death and marriage records. An official certified copy has to be requested from this office.

Sellers meet it at the finish line. Your deed to the buyer is recorded here, together with the electronic transfer return and the fee.

One flat $30 covers a deed no matter how long it is, and the same price applies to mortgages, land contracts and satisfactions.

Document or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage, land contract or satisfaction$30 per document, any number of pages
Subdivision, cemetery or condominium plat$50 per plat
Transportation project plat$30 per plat
Copy of a recorded document$2 for page one, $1 per extra page, and $1 more to certify
Plat copy$5 per page of a plat-size copy, $3 per page of a condominium plat
Real estate transfer fee$3.00 for each $1,000, rounded up to the next hundred

If page one lacks a blank 3 by 3 inch square at the upper right, attach a cover page. The schedule can change, so check with the office before you put a check in the mail.

Under Wisconsin Statute 77.22(1), the grantor, meaning the seller, owes 30 cents on every $100 of value or part thereof, and the register takes the money when the deed is recorded. The county schedule quotes the same charge as $3.00 per $1,000, rounded up to the next hundred.

A transfer return goes with almost every conveyance. Only transfers dated before October 1, 1969 are left out. The return reports value even when no fee is due. Filing is electronic, and a deed without a completed return and the fee will not be accepted. The register does not decide whether a stated value is accurate or an exemption proper.

Statute 77.25 sets out the exemptions. These are the ones that appear most often in house sales and estates:

  • Transfers by will, descent or survivorship.
  • Gifts or token-price transfers inside the family, such as parent to child, stepparent to stepchild or grandparent to grandchild.
  • Foreclosure conveyances and deeds in lieu that go to the mortgage holder or the land contract seller.
  • Real estate worth $1,000 or less.
  • Sales for delinquent taxes or assessments.

The county retains twenty percent of the fees it takes in, and the balance is sent to the state. State the reason for an exemption on the face of the deed, citing the proper subsection of 77.25.

Every deed must follow the standard Wisconsin format in Statute 59.43(2m), in force since September 1, 1996 under Wisconsin Act 110. Pre-printed forms that comply are sold at most office supply stores.

The register's list of rules:

  • Reserve the top right corner, 3 by 3 inches or larger, as blank space for the recording stamp.
  • Type the name and return address just below the stamp area, or at the left inside the top 3 inches.
  • Directly beneath the return address, show the parcel identifier number.
  • Title the document inside the top 3 inches but outside the blank corner.
  • Print on white letter or legal paper of ordinary weight, in ink that scans clearly. The format page allows black, blue or red, and the checklist prefers black.
  • Margins: 1/2 inch at the top of each page, 1/4 inch elsewhere. Hinged pages are not accepted.

If a document was signed outside Wisconsin, a cover sheet can serve as page one with the title, return address and parcel number on it.

Format is only part of it. The register also checks for a full legal description, original signatures with the notary's authentication and a current commission date, the correct fee and a named drafter.

  • The property has to lie within Columbia County.
  • Anything that must be copied, such as the title, return address, names and legal description, has to be legible.
  • Conveyances require the electronic Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return, showing the right fee or an exemption number on deeds and land contracts.
  • One instrument cannot cover several mortgages, assignments or satisfactions.

The intake cutoff for real estate documents is 3:30 p.m., and a package that comes in later waits until the following business day. If the closing hinges on same-day recording, deliver it soon after lunch.

The county offers online access to recorded documents through Fidlar Software's Laredo and Tapestry, and the site mentions xPedite as well. Its tract index only begins January 1, 2006, so anything older requires a grantor and grantee search.

Treat the index as a working tool. It may contain errors, omissions or later changes and should not be relied upon in court or administrative proceedings over title. For an official copy call (608) 742-9677.

Taxes are handled elsewhere. Call the Columbia County Treasurer about what is owed on the parcel while the sale is still open, and find out from the treasurer or the title company how that amount will be paid out of the sale.

Most of the effort comes before you set foot in the Portage office. Here is a sequence to follow during the week of the sale.

  1. Hold the deed up against the format rules, looking at the blank corner, return address and parcel number first.
  2. Make sure the notary's authentication, the commission date and the drafter's name are all present.
  3. Fill in the electronic transfer return, with the sale value or the exemption number.
  4. Set aside the $30 recording fee and the transfer fee.
  5. Get there before 3:30 p.m. if you want same-day recording.

With a cash buyer the same paperwork applies. The lender drops out, which often leaves recording as the final step before the keys change hands.

sections.h2: What a cash sale changes at the recorder
sections.html:
People selling for cash often wonder whether the Portage office treats them differently. It does not. A deed is a deed, and the clerk looks only at the document in front of them: is the corner blank, is the legal description complete, did the notary sign, is the return attached, is the money there.

What does change is the surrounding timeline. Without a mortgage lender, nobody is waiting on a loan package, so the seller and buyer can pick the recording day themselves. Pick a morning, since the 3:30 p.m. cutoff leaves little room for fixes. If the clerk finds a problem with a deed, you can correct it and come back the same day only if the hour allows.

Inherited houses add a step. If the transfer fits an exemption, such as a conveyance by will, descent or survivorship, cite the right subsection of 77.25 on the face of the deed and on the return. If it does not, the fee is figured on the full value, so have the number ready before you reach the counter.

Columbia County lies north of Madison, is mostly rural and counts as part of the Madison metro area. Portage is the seat and biggest city. In 2020 the county had 58,490 residents and 26,565 housing units, with 10.1% vacant and 74.6% of occupied units owner-occupied. Its cities are Columbus (partly in Dodge County), Lodi, Portage and Wisconsin Dells (partly in Adams, Juneau and Sauk counties).

faqs.q: How much does the Columbia County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: It is a flat $30 for each document, however long. That price covers deeds, mortgages, land contracts and satisfactions, and the transfer fee is charged on top.

faqs.q: What is the Columbia County transfer fee rate?
faqs.a: Thirty cents per $100 of value under Wisconsin Statute 77.22(1), which the county schedule writes as $3.00 per $1,000. The seller pays unless the transfer is exempt.

faqs.q: What time does the Columbia County Register of Deeds stop accepting documents for the day?
faqs.a: 3:30 p.m. is the real estate cutoff. Whatever arrives after that is recorded the following business day, though the counter itself stays open longer.

faqs.q: Do I need a transfer return to record a deed in Columbia County?
faqs.a: In nearly every case, yes. File the electronic Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return and include the fee or an exemption number. Value is reported even when the transfer is exempt.

faqs.q: Where do I get a certified copy of a recorded Columbia County deed?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds in Portage is the only source. Pricing is $2 for the first page, $1 for each page after, and $1 to certify. The number to call is (608) 742-9677.
